expectations.text: Starts with ConfigHub-side checks (cub unit get, bridgestate) BEFORE kubectl — ConfigHub is the authoritative owner
expectations.evidence: Step 1 is `cub unit get` + `cub unit bridgestate`; kubectl calls are Step 3.
hello-ns: 3=3=3 (converged). hello-app: 0 vs 6/6 (not converged, explicitly called out).

expectations.text: Correctly identifies that this Target has no controller layer (direct Kubernetes, not Argo/Flux)
expectations.evidence: Step 2 explicitly: 'N/A for this Target — provider is Kubernetes (direct apply), not ArgoCDRenderer or FluxRenderer.'

expectations.text: Uses apply-not-completed filter (or the equivalent LastApplied != Live where-clause) to surface un-converged units
expectations.evidence: `cub unit list --filter platform/apply-not-completed` with where-clause fallback cited.

expectations.text: Names the specific link that broke in plain English (not just 'apply succeeded' or 'apply failed')
expectations.evidence: 'The chain broke at the worker's apply step before the cluster was mutated.'

expectations.text: Stays strictly read-only — no cub unit refresh, no kubectl apply, no argocd sync
expectations.evidence: 'Tool boundary respected' section lists each banned mutation and confirms none called.

expectations.text: Hands off rather than fixing — routes to cub-apply / cub-mutate / triggers-and-applygates instead of re-applying
expectations.evidence: Final hand-off section routes the user, does not retry.
